newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen dropping again on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen dropping again on weak sentiment.

text.p: Thai stocks are seen moving lower on Wednesday following Tuesday's 2.55 percent fall which took the market to its lowest level in 5-1/2 years, analysts said.
The SET Index finished down 16.82 points at 643.28 on Tuesday -- it's lowest close since November 1, 1991. The SET 50 fell 1.37 points, or 2.81 percent, to end at 47.35.

"I'm afraid sentiment is certainly downward. When you see people mentioning support levels at 620-630 and nobody is talking about the market going up, despite what is happening around the region, I'm not optimistic," said Philip Adkins, head of research at Nava SC Securities.
Most regional markets reported strong gains on Tuesday after Wall Street rose to record highs overnight.

But Thailand bucked the trend as a series of economic worries, including lower growth prospects, sluggish exports and concerns surrounding the stability of the finance and property sectors combined to weigh on sentiment, analysts said.
"I think if anything is a relatively safe haven it is the banks. I think most mature investors have already factored in most of the bad news on banking stocks," Adkins said.
Volumes were expected to be thin with international interest likely to be limited, traders said.
Amid this negative environment, Diana Department Store Plc makes its debut on the exchange. The company's initial offer price was 15.50 baht.
